messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for cedarpoint-prod (single-tenant). Streaming endpoints reporting degraded tail latency. Paging on-call: @Maya (oncall).
Maya (oncall): ACK — I'm on it. seeing alert 15:13 UTC. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~450ms, p99 from ~2.3s -> ~8.9s on /v1/stream/generate. Impacting ~6% of requests for cedarpoint-prod. Creating thread.
Omar (eng-sre): On call with you. Any recent deploys? any customer-side spikes in concurrency?
Maya (oncall): No infra deploys in last hour (deploy-bot shows none). Customer is single-tenant ondedicated pool. Metrics: concurrent sessions peaked ~1.2k at spike start. Started 15:12 UTC.
Priya (runtime): I'm pulling runtime traces now. Early signal: KV cache lookup success down from 96% -> 62% for cedarpoint worker pool. Also seeing elevated `stream_write_timeout` logs from streamer threads.
Maya (oncall): Paste logs when you have them.
Priya (runtime): Logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T15:12:23Z] cedarpoint-worker-7 stream_write_timeout session_id=abc123 seq=278 waiting_for_kv_cache
[2026-03-15T15:12:24Z] cedarpoint-worker-3 kv_cache_miss model=redwood-large prefix_hash=0x9f1a2 evicted=true
[2026-03-15T15:12:24Z] cedarpoint-worker-8 stream_flush_delay=320ms
```
Priya (runtime): Also seeing a lot of very long prompt prefixes from the same sessions — multiple multi-turn histories with ~4k token prefixes each. That plus high concurrency looks like it's thrashing prefix/KV cache.
Omar (eng-sre): Can you confirm eviction rate metric? `kv_cache_evictions_total{customer="cedarpoint"}`
Priya (runtime): Evictions spiked ~x14 in the window 15:10-15:16. Checkout this metric snapshot: `kv_cache_evictions_total: 142 -> 1988` and `kv_cache_lookup_success: 0.96 -> 0.62` for cedarpoint pool.
Maya (oncall): Customer impact: Cyrus, can you ping CedarPoint CS? Need to know whether they are seeing user-facing timeouts. @Cyrus (cs)
Cyrus (cs): I'm on a call with customer; they report slow responses and some gRPC timeouts around 15:12-15:20. They have a live feature toggle window. I'll ask them to reduce client concurrency if possible. They're hitting the API with lots of auto-retries.
SupportBot: Noted. Creating incident ticket INC-2026-0315-cedarpoint
Leo (oncall-ml): Quick mitigation options: 1) throttle max concurrency for the customer route, 2) route to fallback smaller model variant (quantized) which uses smaller KV footprint, 3) temporarily increase prefix cache size for their dedicated pool.
Omar (eng-sre): Throttle is fastest. Can we do per-customer routing cap? Maya, can you run the route update?
Maya (oncall): Applying cap now: `redwoodctl routes update --customer cedarpoint --max-concurrency 200` (will push to control-plane). Monitoring.
Maya (oncall): Applied. (command output) `OK: route updated -> max_concurrency=200`
Maya (oncall): Seeing immediate traffic drop to ~180 concurrent sessions for cedarpoint. Re-measuring p95/p99.
Priya (runtime): After cap: p95 ~200ms, p99 ~900ms within 3 minutes — much better than 8.9s. KV cache lookup success recovered to ~88%.
Cyrus (cs): Customer confirmed perceived improvement. They reduced internal retries as requested. Thanks.
Omar (eng-sre): Good triage. Next: need root-cause analysis. Hypothesis: long, high-variance prefixes from many sessions cause cache churn + eviction, amplified by streaming backpressure on writer threads. Also client retry behavior amplifies load.
Leo (oncall-ml): Agreed. Short-term mitigations we did: concurrency cap. Mid-term: consider route fallback to smaller model if prefix cache pressure persists, or pin model variant with smaller KV entry size.
Priya (runtime): I'll spin up a canary in the cedarpoint pool with increased `prefix_cache_size` and add per-customer eviction instrumentation. Running test now: `redwoodctl infra set --pool cedarpoint --prefix-cache-size 1.5x` (dry-run), then will toggle in canary subset.
Omar (eng-sre): I'll run a replay of customer traces in staging to reproduce thrash pattern. Need their example prompts (long histories). Cyrus can you ask for anonymized example payloads?
Cyrus (cs): Requested sample histories; they shared 3 anonymized sessions with ~3.5k token prefixes and heavy system prompts repeated each turn. Uploading to incident ticket.
Maya (oncall): Action items:
- (Priya) instrument per-customer kv_cache_evictions and retention distribution (owner: Priya) — ETA 24h
- (Priya) run canary with increased prefix cache for cedarpoint to validate reduction in evictions — ETA 3h
- (Omar) reproduce offline in staging with sample histories and run load test to verify cache thrash — ETA 6h
- (Maya) keep concurrency cap in place and monitor for 12h; if stable, we can ramp slowly — ETA 12h
- (Cyrus) notify customer of mitigations and ask for client-side retry/backoff changes — ETA 30m
- (Leo) prepare rollback/fallback plan: route to quantized model variant if cache mitigation fails — ETA 6h
Maya (oncall): Creating follow-up ticket + doc: /confluence/incidents/cedarpoint-2026-03-15 (incident stub). Adding next-oncall handoff notes.
Priya (runtime): Note: we also observed `stream_write_backpressure` in some workers; I'll add extra logging around streamer queue depths to correlate.
Omar (eng-sre): For postmortem: consider autoscaling policy for dedicated pools under extreme prefix-size workloads and a per-customer prefix-cache quota.
Maya (oncall): Handoff: I'm handing off to @Leo (oncall-ml) for night shift. Summary: concurrency cap applied, customer impact reduced, investigating kv cache thrash caused by very long prefixes + high concurrency. See action items above. Please escalate to infra if evictions persist.
Leo (oncall-ml): ACK and taking over for next 8h. I'll watch `p99`, `kv_cache_evictions_total{customer="cedarpoint"}`, and streamer queue depths. Will update thread every hour or on any regression.
Cyrus (cs): Thanks team. I'll follow up with customer postmortem once root cause confirmed.
Maya (oncall): Marking incident as "mitigated" for now, keeping ticket open. :white_check_mark:
SupportBot: INC-2026-0315-cedarpoint updated: status=mitigated, severity=high, assignees=[Maya, Priya, Omar, Leo, Cyrus]
Maya (oncall): Leaving final note before sign-off: if eviction rate doesn't fall below 200/min after canary, we should plan for fallback route to smaller model overnight. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
